source.title: Evolving Jailbreaks: Automated Multi-Objective Long-Tail Attacks on Large Language Models
source.authors: W. Hong; Zhong-Hua Rong; Li Wang; Feng-Cheng Chang; Jian Zhu; Ke Tang; Zexuan Zhu; Y. Ong

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling, truncation, or wrong-document issue.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports long-tail jailbreak attack results, but does not test the fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant-prefill, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports hypervolume scores combining attack success rate and output perplexity, but those aggregate scores do not isolate a measure named by any claim version. It also presents qualitative attack outputs and descriptions for two LLaMA-7B examples; these are recorded below as findings about long-tail attacks, not as tests of the listed claims. The initialization, mutation, crossover, and repair prompts are instructions to the study's design model, not to an AI reading or reviewing this text.
record.test_reason: This is a jailbreak-method paper. EvoJail uses evolved encryption-decryption prompts and is scored by hypervolume over ASR and perplexity against six baseline attacks. It does no fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no prefilling, suffix or decoding manipulation, no parameter localization and no deepening. Its only link to the claim is a citation of Qi et al. (the 'few tokens deep' paper) among future-work references in the conclusion. Encoded-prompt attacks are not the prefill, suffix or decoding mechanism V4 names, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that EvoJail is the first automated multi-objective framework for long-tail jailbreaks. They say it achieves competitive attack effectiveness and superior output quality (low perplexity), with a diverse Pareto front. They offer it as a tool for assessing LLM safety and motivating adaptive defenses.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses multi-objective evolutionary search to generate reversible encryption-decryption prompts; it does not fine-tune models or measure aligned-versus-base token-position KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack outcomes vary by model and scenario; the paper notes that GPT-G remains dominated by CodeAttack even as EvoJail's ensemble size increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Evolved encryption-decryption prompts elicit harmful multi-step plans from Llama-2-7b-chat in two illustrated cases, where several baseline encoded attacks are refused. Hypervolume (ASR plus perplexity) favours EvoJail in 15 of 18 scenarios.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Long-tail encoded jailbreak prompts can bypass refusal in chat models, with success depending on the attack and the target model.

record.problems: The qualitative examples cover two prompts on one model and do not establish general attack rates. The main reported aggregate metric is hypervolume, which combines attack effectiveness and output perplexity rather than reporting isolated values here. The paper mentions averages across independent runs but gives no uncertainty estimates in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 hypervolume values and the ensemble-scale plots were not recorded as rows because they aggregate attack success and output perplexity and do not isolate a measure named by any claim version.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes; only encoded-prompt attacks are tested.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'discusses' is too strong: the paper only cites the original source (ref 32) in passing in the conclusion, so 'cites_only' fits better. All rows are the study's own method compared with baselines, which this verdict step says should be flagged. Hypervolume tables mix ASR and PPL and cannot isolate harmful-compliance rates, so leaving them out is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests long-tail encoded prompts, not compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes to the model.
